summary.headline: Diamond Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 129% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT rose 191% to INR58.5 crores, with FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR690 crores (up 129% YoY), EBITDA INR85 crores (12.3% margin, up ~200 bps) and PAT INR58.5 crores (8.5% margin). Management attributed the quarter's softness versus a normal Q1 to early, heavy monsoon flooding in Gujarat that hit medium and extra high voltage cable laying. The company completed a INR1,640 crore QIP (net INR1,614 crore), turning net worth positive at INR691 crore post-QIP from negative INR922 crore at June 30, 2026. Order book stood at INR3,688 crore as on August 11, 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore and FY28 of INR7,500 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Negative INR922 crore at 30 Jun 2026; positive INR691 crore post-QIP
INR1,640 crore gross (INR1,614 crore net per Q&A)
INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 (~$445 mn), across 12 product lines
financial_highlights.change: ~2x FY26 revenue; >INR1,000 crore fresh wins since April

financial_highlights.value: Negligible in Q1 due to carried-forward losses; benefit expected for at least two years

segments.name: Medium voltage (11–66 kV) and EHV (132 kV+) cables
segments.commentary: Largest order-book block; management targets moving mix up the voltage curve, with 66 kV and above EBITDA guided at 18–22%. A INR435 crore data center order sits in this band.

segments.name: Low voltage (1.1 kV) cables
segments.commentary: Q1 mix skewed toward LV and conductors because MV/EHV cannot be laid in flood conditions; LV EBITDA guided at 8–9%. New copper LV facility (brownfield, ~42,000 km capacity, revenue potential ~INR1,880 crore) targeted for FY28 commercial production.

segments.name: Conductors (incl. HTLS, AL-59)
segments.commentary: Conductor EBITDA guided at 9–10%. Management says AL-59 is now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped producing ACSR.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Currently negligible. Team being built; certifications for Europe and US in progress. Internal target of INR500 crore export order book by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the fourth rod mill, the incremental silane line and the CCV line, and sixth CCV line delivery.
qa_highlights.answer: Rod mill by 15 Oct, silane line by 15 Sep, CCV line in March 2027; sixth CCV line to be ordered this month, delivery assurance for August 2027 and commissioning by December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Net worth and use of QIP proceeds.
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth was negative INR922 crore at 30 June 2026 and is positive INR691 crore after the INR1,614 crore net QIP proceeds. Planned use: INR130 crore LV expansion, INR74 crore balancing equipment, INR325 crore general corporate purposes, INR350 crore promoter unsecured loan repayment, with about INR750 crore for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery expectation on the INR957 crore legacy receivables.
qa_highlights.answer: A special team is evaluating recovery; management expects about INR300 crore to be recovered over 12–18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation outlook after the audit qualification was resolved.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 depreciation will be the run-rate going forward, with pro-rata additions for new capex.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 phasing and utilisation for cables and conductors.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp will be gradual, with Q2 partly affected by rain and Q3–Q4 the strongest; utilisation is guided at ~40% for conductors and ~50–52% for cables in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin guidance and metal price sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 11–13% EBITDA margin, depending on metal prices; management cited aluminium moving from about $3,800 in May to about $3,000 by end-June. Mix is expected to improve as MV and EHV volumes rise in Q2–Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term debt and peak debt outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no substantial debt, the INR400 crore promoter unsecured loan has been repaid post-QIP and the INR1,900 crore promoter-held bonds are 0.01% payable after 30 years, with a net present value of INR47 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peer comparison given the flat Q-o-Q revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 softness to MV/EHV being laid at project sites that cannot be laid in rain, and said the peers' business is largely LV, so the cycle hits Diamond more.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration, including Adani.
qa_highlights.answer: Adani is about 40%+ of the order book, with a Board mandate to cut it to about 20% by year-end; the company is engaging about 670 active customers.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix at the INR14,000 crore peak and what could go wrong.
qa_highlights.answer: Conductors 30–35%, LV 10–15%, MV/EHV the remainder; data center target 20%, exports not yet sized beyond INR500 crore order target. Key risks are metal and polymer price moves requiring 20–30% more working capital, and execution capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crore, with management saying it is firmly on track and intends to hold the Q1 margin profile while delivering it.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 11–13%, dependent on metal prices; management said the absolute contribution stays steady under price-escalation contracts.
Q1 seasonality: management said an on-time monsoon would have added INR70–80 crore of top line and corresponding EBITDA in Q1.
FY28 revenue target of INR7,500 crore; management said the full-utilisation potential of INR14,000 crore is not expected in FY29.
Data center sales targeted at about INR750 crore in FY27 and INR1,500 crore in FY28 (about 20% of revenue); internal target of INR1,000 crore data center orders before 31 Mar 2027.
Export order book target of at least INR500 crore by year-end FY27; management said export guidance beyond this will be given after year-end.
Management said it expects around INR300 crore of legacy NCLT receivables (out of INR957 crore) to be recovered over 12–18 months.
capex_capacity: Two aluminium corrugation lines approved by the board for 66 kV and 132 kV cable capacity; capex about INR17 crore, achieved by converting one 33 kV line.

Sixth CCV line being ordered this month at an agreed price; delivery assurance for August 2027, commissioning expected by December 2027 with no additional civil or utility capex. Management said it triples capability in the target segment.

Two additional medium voltage cable lines under installation, said to be on schedule; one silane line expected by 15 Sep 2026, fourth rod mill by 15 Oct 2026, and one CCV line in March 2027 (per Q&A).

Copper LV and control cable facility converting old rod mill and legacy conductor plant (brownfield, no civil cost), about 42,000 km capacity and revenue potential about INR1,880 crore at full utilisation; commercial production FY28, commissioning before March 2027.

Capex per line per Q&A: silane line INR15–20 crore; CCV line about INR50 crore for the line plus about INR50 crore utilities and civil (about INR100 crore total), with revenue of about INR45–50 crore per line. Utilisation guided at conductors ~40% and cables ~50–52% in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.
demand_pricing: Order book INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 across 12 product lines, about 2x last year's revenue; over INR1,000 crore of fresh wins since April and about INR400 crore of orders in the last 6–7 days.
Order intake guided at INR275–325 crore per month; management said about INR2,800 crore of the book is to be executed before March 2027.
Adani Group share of the order book about 40%+, with a Board mandate to bring it to about 20% by year-end; around 670 active customers and 200+ in the current order book.

Gujarat disaster-management programme (Robust) estimated at INR22,000 crore over three years, of which INR16,000 crore is 11 kV and 33 kV MV cable; Rajesh Power 1,370 km order from Paschim Gujarat; management expects INR4,000–5,000 crore of Gujarat orders to be finalised by year-end.

Mix: management said MV and EHV cannot be laid in flooded sites, so Q1 skewed to LV and conductors; management said peers are mostly ~85% LV, whereas Diamond is ~70–80% MV/EHV. Conductor: AL-59 now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped making ACSR.
risks_watch: Phasing: FY27 guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore implies INR1,200–1,250 crore per quarter for Q2–Q4 against INR690 crore in Q1. Watch Q2 revenue.
Metal and polymer price volatility affecting gross margin and the pass-through lag; management's margin range is 11–13%.
Commissioning timelines: silane line (15 Sep 2026), rod mill (15 Oct 2026), CCV lines in March 2027 and December 2027; the new LV facility is due by March 2027 and commercial output in FY28.
Export certifications for Europe and the US; first export order targeted by Q3–Q4 FY27.
Working capital needs rising with metal and polymer costs and the need for vendor and dealer financing.
Customer concentration: Adani at 40%+ of the order book against the 20% target.
Monsoon and project-site disruption affecting MV/EHV laying in Q2 (described as partially affected).
key_quotes: We are completely back-to-back on passing the increases in metal and polymers to all our customers.
Our guidance is between 11% to 13%. This again depends upon the metal price.
The EBITDA guidance for the next year, we are confident we will maintain it between what I am telling you today, but we will work on how to improve upon it.
So, the rod mill should start by 15th of October. The incremental MV silane line should start somewhere by 15th of September, and the CCV line will start in March 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, capacity and the FY27/FY28 targets, but measured on guidance specifics: the CEO-style speaker declined to give firm forward-looking assurances at the outset and repeatedly hedged margin and export numbers with metal-price and utilisation caveats. Tone was most defensive when addressing the Q-o-Q flatness versus peers and the Adani concentration.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300-4,500 crore against FY26 base (~INR2,800-2,900 crore implied by 54% midpoint), backed by order book of INR3,688 crore (~2x last year's revenue), multiple capacity lines coming live and a copper LV facility for FY28 with utilisation at 34%.
